atomic_findings.regression_test: The response's 'Reported chain' matrix row (bytes 3307-3548) proposes: build A (attrs, frozen on_setattr), non-attrs B(A) with no setter, mutable attrs C(B), for both slots=False and slots=True; expected result is explicit: assignment to C.x succeeds, C.__setattr__ is object.__setattr__, and C.__attrs_own_setattr__ is false. This uses only APIs present in the pinned packet evidence (attr.s, attr.ib, on_setattr, setters.frozen, __attrs_own_setattr__, object.__setattr__) and its expected outcome is exactly the de-xfailed success condition of the pinned test_slotted_confused; the boundary row at bytes 3873-4054 (user-owned intermediate __setattr__ must be preserved) matches pinned test_setattr_inherited_do_not_reset. No invented API or contract.
atomic_findings.residue: When inherited behavior carries an ownership marker, decide whether to remove it by locating the effective method provider first (first class in MRO attribute-resolution order whose own __dict__ contains __setattr__), then read the ownership marker from that provider's own namespace; never keep searching past a user-owned provider. Falsifiable as stated at bytes 5614-6334: a hierarchy where the rule selects a different provider than Python's actual __setattr__ lookup, or where it replaces an effective user-owned setter, disproves it.
atomic_findings.applicability_predicate: Applies only to machinery where method ownership is reliably represented on the method-defining class's own namespace (e.g. attrs' __attrs_own_setattr__ marker on classes defining an attrs-generated __setattr__), for both slotted and dict-backed class construction paths, resolved by ordinary class-dictionary/MRO lookup.
exclusions: Methods or ownership markers mutated independently after class creation
Methods supplied dynamically by a metaclass without an owning class-dictionary entry
Resolution mechanisms not represented by ordinary class-dictionary/MRO lookup
